subject: Educational Psychology
stem: According to Herzberg's two-factor theory (applied to workplace/classroom motivation), factors like salary or basic working conditions that prevent dissatisfaction but do not by themselves create true motivation are called:
explanation: Herzberg distinguished 'hygiene factors' (pay, conditions — prevent dissatisfaction but don't motivate) from 'motivators' (achievement, recognition, growth — which genuinely drive motivation and satisfaction).

subject: Educational Psychology
stem: A student who believes 'my exam results depend mostly on my own effort and preparation' is displaying:
explanation: Internal locus of control is the belief that outcomes result from one's own actions/effort. External locus attributes outcomes to luck, fate or other people — generally associated with lower academic motivation.

section: Educational Psychology · Ch9 — Motivation — Deep Practice
subject: Educational Psychology
stem: A student who has repeatedly failed despite trying hard eventually stops attempting even easy tasks, believing 'nothing I do will help'. This pattern is called:
explanation: Learned helplessness (Seligman) develops when repeated failure/lack of control leads a person to stop trying even when success is possible — the opposite of high self-efficacy.
